label: PF Backlog 590
title: EDP-09: Tenant context service with server-side membership/role verification + RLS (USING + WITH CHECK) + pooled-context negative tests
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.

brief.problem: Application relies on application-layer tenant filtering; a code bug or SQL injection could expose cross-tenant data.
brief.what_adds: Server-side membership verification and PostgreSQL RLS with USING + WITH CHECK, plus negative tests proving pooled connections cannot leak tenant context.
brief.why: RLS provides defense-in-depth at the database layer so even compromised application code cannot read another tenant's data.
brief.who_feels: Security teams (hard isolation guarantee), enterprise customers (data privacy), auditors (evidence of row-level controls).

objective: Build a tenant context service in Go that enforces server-side membership/role verification, applies PostgreSQL RLS (USING + WITH CHECK) on tenant-scoped tables, and includes pooled-connection negative tests to prevent cross-tenant leakage.
acceptance_criteria: TenantContextService validates membership/role against database on each request
RLS policies with USING and WITH CHECK created via migration for all tenant-scoped tables
Pooled connection negative tests confirm stale context is rejected and no cross-tenant data leaks
config/context-policy.json extended with tenant isolation settings
Language rule review passes (Go-only)
in_scope: RLS migration with USING + WITH CHECK policies
out_of_scope: Tenant CRUD and membership management APIs (BI-PF-1296)
approach: Define TenantContextService, implement membership verification query, create RLS migrations using migration framework from BI-PF-1300, build negative tests with connection pool scenarios.
verification: Negative test: stale tenant context rejected (403 or RLS filtering)
Negative test: cross-tenant SELECT returns zero rows
RLS policies verified via pg_policies query in integration test
risks: RLS USING + WITH CHECK on all tables increases migration complexity
Pooled connections leaking tenant context between requests is a critical security risk
Performance impact of server-side membership verification on every request
rollback: Disable RLS policies via migration and revert service package; existing application-level tenant filtering continues to operate.
evidence: Existing tenant APIs confirm tenant/membership model
core/context_discipline.py shows context validation precedents in codebase

analysis.implementation_strategy: Create Go package `internal/tenantcontext/` with a TenantContextService that validates server-side membership/role on every request and sets PostgreSQL session variables for RLS. Define RLS policies with both USING and WITH CHECK clauses via migrations (consumes BI-PF-1300 migration framework). Build pooled-context negative tests that verify stale/wrong-tenant contexts are rejected. Extend config/context-policy.json with tenant isolation settings.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-1296 (tenant service) — membership/role data source
REQUIRES BI-PF-1300 (migration framework) — RLS policies applied via migrations
RELATED BI-PF-1299 (storage interfaces) — context flows through storage abstraction
RELATED BI-PF-1303 (ResidencyPolicy) — residency enforcement interacts with tenant isolation
conflict_findings: BI-PF-1300 creates migration framework; RLS migrations must be sequenced after role creation
BI-PF-1303 RegionCell attestation may also set session context — coordinate session variable ownership
duplication_findings: core/context_policy.py and config/context-policy.json provide context-policy patterns but in Python — reusable as config schema only
Existing tenant APIs (/api/v1/enterprise/tenants/*) confirm tenant model exists — reuse membership/role data model
core/context_preflight.py preflight-check pattern relevant for context validation design
analysis.rationale: Tenant isolation via RLS is a critical enterprise security control. No existing Go implementation exists; new package required. Existing Python context-policy patterns inform config schema only.
assumptions: PostgreSQL RLS is the enforcement mechanism
Tenant membership/role is stored in a database table accessible by the verification query
Connection pooling uses a library that supports per-request session setup/teardown
risks: RLS USING + WITH CHECK on all tables increases migration complexity
Pooled connections leaking tenant context between requests is a critical security risk
Performance impact of server-side membership verification on every request
evidence: Existing tenant APIs confirm tenant/membership model
core/context_discipline.py shows context validation precedents in codebase
missing_info: Whether tenant context is per-request or per-session

context_review.reason: Conceptually clear but depends on migration framework (1300) and tenant service (1296). RLS table inventory needs enumeration during implementation.

consolidation_proposal.title: EDP-09: Tenant context service with server-side membership/role verification + RLS (USING + WITH CHECK) + pooled-context negative tests
consolidation_proposal.body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant membership/roles resolved from identity/token, never trusted from headers; X-Tenant-Id is a selector only.
Tenant-owned tables use RLS with USING + WITH CHECK and default deny; runtime role cannot bypass.
Transaction-local tenant context is cleared between pooled requests; negative tests prove no bleed.
cross_tenant_allowed is wired at the API boundary.
ADR document committed covering storage layers, backends, and data-flow decisions
Develop commit SHA pinned and recorded
L1 Go rule passes language_rule_review.py
11 Go interfaces defined in internal/storage/ with godoc and compile-time assertions
Conformance harness package exposes embeddable test suites per interface
In-memory reference adapter passes all conformance suites
scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py passes (Go-only)
config/test-matrix.json extended with storage-conformance rows
private buckets, least-privilege credentials, lifecycle/versioning where required; explicit region/backup/replication capability metadata.
Signed URLs only after authorization, constrained to object/method, short TTL.
Provider config stays inside the adapter; conformance suite passes (wrong-region, versions, delete, restore).
tenant.home_region, jurisdiction_profile_id, residency_policy_version are set at provisioning from authenticated config (never from X-Tenant-Id/X-Region/URL).
Provisioning fails closed if any required service (DB/object/backup/logs/KMS/queue/cache/vector/workers/model) lacks an approved region.
Region is immutable to ordinary users; changes require an audited migration plan.
